neighbours.label: The indefinite place adverbs ' somewhere', ' anywhere', ' elsewhere', ' everywhere' (and weaker ' wherever'), in any context; peaks strongest on ' somewhere' and ' anywhere'
fire: My brother left his car keys somewhere in the garden and spent all morning searching.
Scientists believe the signal originated somewhere near the center of the galaxy.
There was a quieter campsite somewhere further up the valley, according to the ranger.
The cat refuses to sleep anywhere except on the warm laptop keyboard.
Few restaurants anywhere in the state can match their seafood chowder.
Unhappy with the service, the couple decided to eat elsewhere that evening.
In spring the pollen gets everywhere, coating cars and windowsills in yellow dust.
The toddler follows his older sister wherever she goes around the house.
quiet: My brother left his car keys on the kitchen counter and spent all morning searching.
Scientists believe the signal originated near the center of a distant galaxy.
There was a quieter campsite further up the valley, according to the old map.
The cat refuses to sleep on any surface except the warm laptop keyboard.
Few restaurants in the whole state can match their famous seafood chowder.
Unhappy with the service, the couple decided to cook at home that evening.
In spring the pollen coats every car and windowsill on the block in yellow dust.
The toddler follows his older sister into every room of the house.
